# Appendix F: Diagnostics

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_appendix_f.py from book/appendices/appendix-f.intro.md, appendix-f.lines.txt, src/diagnostics/catalog.cee and the chapters' `diagnostics:` headers; edit those, not this page. -->

This appendix lists every diagnostic code of `ceesafec` %ceesafec-version%: 154 errors and 5 warnings. Find the code from your
message (`error[N0249]`) in the tables, which are in the order of the numbers. Each row says what went wrong and the
usual fix, and links to the sections of the book that show the diagnostic in a listing, with its message and the
corrected program. A code that no section shows links to its table in the specification.

## How to read a diagnostic

This program leaves out `mut` in a call:

<!-- ceesafe: fail N0249 -->
```ceesafe
fn main() {
    var line = String.create();
    if (Console.readLine(line)!) {
        Console.writeLine(line);
    }
}
```

```text
main.cee:3:26: error[N0249]: this parameter is 'borrow mut': write 'mut' before the argument to let the call modify it
  |
3 |     if (Console.readLine(line)!) {
  |                          ^^^^
```

The parts of the first line, in order:

| Part | Here | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| The place | `main.cee:3:26` | The file, the line and the column where the fault starts. Both count from 1. |
| The kind | `error` | `error` or `warning`. An error stops the command. A warning does not. |
| The code | `N0249` | The diagnostic's code. It never changes its meaning from one release to the next. |
| The message | `this parameter is …` | What is wrong in this program, with its names and types. One code can have several messages. |

Under it is the source line, with `^` marks under the part the diagnostic is about. Some diagnostics have notes
after that, each with its own place: where a value was moved, where a borrow was taken.
[Hello, world](./ch01-02-hello-world) reads a first message in full, and [Borrowing](./ch04-02-borrowing) one with a
note.

Diagnostics come in the order the compiler finds them. Correct the first one first: a later one is often a
result of it.

### `ceesafec explain`

`ceesafec explain` prints what a code means, with an example, from the specification inside the compiler. It needs
no network ([1.1](./ch01-01-installation)).

```sh
$ ceesafec explain N0249
N0249: `mut` argument marker missing or misplaced
example: `take(x)` for `borrow mut`, `look(mut x)` for `borrow`
```

For some codes it also prints the specification's paragraphs that name the code.

### `ceesafec fix`

Where only one repair is possible, the compiler offers it as a fix. `ceesafec fix` applies every fix to the files,
checks again, and repeats until no fix is left. Then it prints the diagnostics that remain. `ceesafec fix --dry-run`
changes no file, and prints the edits:

```sh
$ ceesafec fix --dry-run main.cee
main.cee:3:26: write 'mut' before the argument: '' -> 'mut '
```

Release %ceesafec-version% has fixes for six codes: N0100 (a missing `;`), N0201 (an extern declaration that repeats a
dependency's), N0208 (`as` to `truncate`), N0211 and N0248 (`let` to `var`), and N0249 (`mut` added or removed). No
chapter of the book teaches `fix`. The page
[The ceesafec command](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/guide/ceesafec) of the guide does.

### `--diagnostics-format=json`

A program that reads diagnostics, an AI model among them, asks for them as JSON. With
`--diagnostics-format=json`, the commands `check`, `build`, `run` and `fix` write one JSON document, on one line,
to standard output. For the program above:

```sh
$ ceesafec check --diagnostics-format=json main.cee
{"version":1,"errors":1,"warnings":0,"diagnostics":[{"code":"N0249","severity":"error","file":"main.cee","start":{"line":3,"column":26},"end":{"line":3,"column":30},"message":"this parameter is 'borrow mut': write 'mut' before the argument to let the call modify it","summary":"`mut` argument marker missing or misplaced","notes":[],"fixes":[{"title":"write 'mut' before the argument","edits":[{"file":"main.cee","start":{"line":3,"column":26},"end":{"line":3,"column":26},"newText":"mut "}]}]}]}
```

Each diagnostic has its `code`, its `severity`, its place (`file`, `start`, and `end`, which is the position after
the last character), the `message`, the code's one-line `summary`, its `notes` and its `fixes`, each fix a list of
edits. The specification gives the format in full:
[Tooling, section 5](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/tooling). The options of each command are in
[Appendix E](./appendix-e-ceesafec).

## How to read the tables

- **Code.** The tables are in the order of the numbers, in the groups of the specification. Search the page for
  your code.
- **Kind.** `error` or `warning`.
- **What went wrong, and the usual fix.** One line in the book's words. The compiler's message for your program
  says more, and `ceesafec explain` gives the specification's wording.
- **Shown in.** The sections with a listing that produces the diagnostic, by number: `4.2` is chapter 4, section
  2. For a code that no section shows, the link goes to the code's table in
  [the specification's list of diagnostics](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics).

## Lexer (N0001 to N0011)

The lexer cuts a file into tokens - names, numbers, literals, operators. It finishes a file before the parser starts, so these come first among a file's diagnostics.

| Code | Kind | What went wrong, and the usual fix | Shown in |
|---|---|---|---|
| N0001 | error | A character that starts no token, such as `#`, or a letter that is not ASCII outside a literal or a comment. Remove it, or put the text in a string literal. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#lexer-n0001%E2%80%93n0099) |
| N0003 | error | A block comment opened with `/*` is never closed. Add the `*/`. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#lexer-n0001%E2%80%93n0099) |
| N0004 | error | An integer literal does not fit in 64 bits. Write a smaller number. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#lexer-n0001%E2%80%93n0099) |
| N0005 | error | A string literal has no closing `"` before the end of its line or of the file. Close it, or use a raw `"""` literal for text of several lines. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#lexer-n0001%E2%80%93n0099) |
| N0006 | error | A literal has an escape that does not exist (`"\q"`), a `\u{...}` that is not a Unicode scalar value, or a NUL byte in a `c"…"` literal. Use an escape the language has. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#lexer-n0001%E2%80%93n0099) |
| N0007 | error | A character literal is empty, holds more than one character, or is not closed. Write one character between the `'` marks, and use a string literal for text. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#lexer-n0001%E2%80%93n0099) |
| N0008 | error | A number literal has a digit its radix does not have (`0b102`), or a radix prefix with no digits (`0x`). Correct the digits. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#lexer-n0001%E2%80%93n0099) |
| N0009 | error | A number literal ends in a suffix that is not a type it can have (`12abc`, `1f32`). Use an integer type's name on an integer literal, and a float type's on a float literal, `1.0f32`. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#lexer-n0001%E2%80%93n0099) |
| N0010 | error | A digit separator `_` is not between two digits (`1__0`, `0x_FF`, `1_.5`). Put each `_` between two digits. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#lexer-n0001%E2%80%93n0099) |
| N0011 | error | A raw `"""` string literal is laid out wrongly - text follows the opening `"""` on its line, or a line of the text is indented less than the closing `"""`. Start the text on the next line, and indent it at least as far as the closing `"""`. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#lexer-n0001%E2%80%93n0099) |

## Parser (N0100 to N0110)

The parser reports one diagnostic for each broken statement or item, and goes on at the next one. The rules after this group are checked only when every file parses.

| Code | Kind | What went wrong, and the usual fix | Shown in |
|---|---|---|---|
| N0100 | error | The parser needed one particular token and found another, most often a missing `;`, `(` or `}`. The message names the token it expected. A `fn` in an enum's body gives this too, since an enum's functions go in an `impl` block. | [1.2](./ch01-02-hello-world), [3.2](./ch03-02-data-types), [3.3](./ch03-03-functions), [3.4](./ch03-04-comments), [3.5](./ch03-05-control-flow), [5.1](./ch05-01-defining-structs), [6.1](./ch06-01-defining-an-enum), [6.2](./ch06-02-match), [6.3](./ch06-03-optionals), [19.1](./ch19-01-where-patterns-go) |
| N0101 | error | Something that is not an item stands at the top level of a file, such as a `let` or another statement. Move it into a function, or declare a `const`. | [3.2](./ch03-02-data-types) |
| N0102 | error | An expression is missing where one is needed (`let a = ;`). Write the value. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#parser-n0100%E2%80%93n0199) |
| N0103 | error | Comparison operators are chained (`a < b < c`). Write two comparisons joined by `&&`. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#parser-n0100%E2%80%93n0199) |
| N0104 | error | The left side of an assignment cannot be assigned (`1 = 2;`, `f() = 3;`). Assign to a variable, a field or an element. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#parser-n0100%E2%80%93n0199) |
| N0105 | error | A type is missing where one is needed (`fn f(x: ) {}`), or `Self` is written outside an interface, an `impl` and a struct's or enum's body. Write the type's name. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#parser-n0100%E2%80%93n0199) |
| N0106 | error | A `namespace` declaration is not the first thing in its file. Move it to the top. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#parser-n0100%E2%80%93n0199) |
| N0107 | error | A struct's body holds something that is not a field or a `fn` (`struct A { 42; }`), or an imported C union has no member. Write each field as `name: Type;`. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#parser-n0100%E2%80%93n0199) |
| N0108 | error | A `match` arm starts with something that is not a pattern (`+ => …`). Write `_`, a literal, a range, a name, `name @ P`, `[…]` or a variant such as `E.V(…)`. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#parser-n0100%E2%80%93n0199) |
| N0109 | error | An `import` declaration comes after an item. Move every `import` above the first item of the file. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#parser-n0100%E2%80%93n0199) |
| N0110 | error | The source is nested more than 1,000 levels deep (blocks, parentheses, or one chain of operators or calls), and the rest of the file is not parsed. Split the expression or the function. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#parser-n0100%E2%80%93n0199) |

## Names, types and flow (N0200 to N0236)

The type checker's diagnostics - names, types, constants, assignments, and the paths through a function.

| Code | Kind | What went wrong, and the usual fix | Shown in |
|---|---|---|---|
| N0200 | error | A name that nothing declares - a variable, a function, or a member of a built-in type (`Console.print`). Check the spelling - the message suggests names that exist. | [1.3](./ch01-03-hello-package), [3.1](./ch03-01-variables), [5.3](./ch05-03-methods), [6.1](./ch06-01-defining-an-enum), [11.3](./ch11-03-organising-tests), [13.2](./ch13-02-iteration), [19.1](./ch19-01-where-patterns-go) |
| N0201 | error | Two items of the package have one name, two C declarations have one C name, or an item takes a reserved built-in name such as `Result` or `Box`. Rename one. | [7.2](./ch07-02-files-and-public) |
| N0202 | error | Two parameters of a function have one name. Rename one. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#names-types-and-flow-n0200%E2%80%93n0299) |
| N0203 | error | A `let` or `var` declares a name that a local or parameter in scope already has. CeeSafe has no shadowing of locals, so choose another name, or assign to the existing `var`. | [3.1](./ch03-01-variables), [19.3](./ch19-03-the-syntax-whole) |
| N0204 | error | A type name that nothing declares (`int`), or a generic type without its type arguments or with the wrong number of them. Use the real name (`i32`), or import the package that declares it. | [7.3](./ch07-03-imports) |
| N0205 | error | A value has another type than its place needs (`let a: bool = 1;`, `if (n)` with a number). CeeSafe converts nothing silently, so convert the value yourself, or change the declared type. | [3.2](./ch03-02-data-types), [3.5](./ch03-05-control-flow), [8.1](./ch08-01-vectors), [8.2](./ch08-02-strings), [8.3](./ch08-03-maps), [12.1](./ch12-01-arguments), [12.5](./ch12-05-environment), [12.6](./ch12-06-standard-error), [13.2](./ch13-02-iteration), [17.3](./ch17-03-timeouts-races-cancellation), [18.1](./ch18-01-dynamic-dispatch), [18.2](./ch18-02-when-to-use-it) |
| N0206 | error | An integer literal does not fit its type (`256u8`, `let c: i8 = 128;`). Use a wider type or a smaller value. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#names-types-and-flow-n0200%E2%80%93n0299) |
| N0207 | error | An operator is used on types it does not take - two different integer types (`u8` and `i32`), a bitwise operator on a signed integer, `-` on an unsigned one, or `==` on a struct or an enum with payloads. Convert one operand so that both have one type, or give the type its `==` with `@derive(Equal)`. | [2](./ch02-00-guessing-game), [3.2](./ch03-02-data-types), [5.1](./ch05-01-defining-structs), [5.2](./ch05-02-example-structs), [6.1](./ch06-01-defining-an-enum), [6.3](./ch06-03-optionals), [8.2](./ch08-02-strings), [10.1](./ch10-01-generic-types), [12.2](./ch12-02-reading-a-file), [20.4](./ch20-04-arithmetic), [20.5](./ch20-05-derives-and-macros) |
| N0208 | error | An `as` conversion could lose information (`a as u32` with `a: i32`). Use `truncate<T>(x)` to wrap, or `checkedTruncate` or `saturatingTruncate` to check or clamp. | [3.2](./ch03-02-data-types) |
| N0209 | error | A call has the wrong number of arguments, or `Ok` or `Err` the wrong number of values. Give exactly what the declaration takes. | [21.4](./ch21-04-async-tasks) |
| N0210 | error | Something that is not a function is called (`local()`), or a function or built-in is used as a value where it cannot be. Call only functions and closures. | [20.5](./ch20-05-derives-and-macros) |
| N0211 | error | An assignment to something that cannot change - a `let` local, a parameter, a constant, or an element of a `let` array. Declare the variable with `var`. | [3.1](./ch03-01-variables), [3.3](./ch03-03-functions), [5.1](./ch05-01-defining-structs), [15.1](./ch15-01-box), [15.4](./ch15-04-cells), [15.5](./ch15-05-shared-ownership) |
| N0212 | error | A local is read before every path has given it a value (`var x: i32; return x;`). Give it a value at its declaration, or on each path before the read. | [3.1](./ch03-01-variables) |
| N0213 | error | A function that returns a value can reach its end without a `return`, or the `else` block of a `let … else` can finish without leaving. End every path with `return`, and make the `else` block leave. | [3.3](./ch03-03-functions) |
| N0214 | error | `break` or `continue` is outside a loop. Remove it, or move it into the loop. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#names-types-and-flow-n0200%E2%80%93n0299) |
| N0215 | error | A `return` does not agree with the function's return type - a value in a `void` function, no value in a function that returns one, or any `return` in a `never` function. Change the `return` or the return type. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#names-types-and-flow-n0200%E2%80%93n0299) |
| N0216 | error | A construct the compiler does not support where it is written, such as a constant of a raw pointer type, or region parameters on an interface's method. The message says which. The code also reports an internal fault of `ceesafec`. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#names-types-and-flow-n0200%E2%80%93n0299) |
| N0217 | error | A constant's value, or arithmetic on literals anywhere, is not a constant expression or would panic when evaluated (`const C: u8 = 200 + 100;`). Use a value that fits the type, or compute it at run time. | [20.4](./ch20-04-arithmetic) |
| N0218 | error | A constant's value depends on the constant itself (`const A: i32 = A + 1;`). Break the cycle. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#names-types-and-flow-n0200%E2%80%93n0299) |
| N0219 | error | `main` has a signature it cannot have - parameters, type parameters, `async` or `unsafe`. Write `fn main()` or `fn main() -> i32`. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#names-types-and-flow-n0200%E2%80%93n0299) |
| N0220 | error | A `let` has no initialiser (`let a: i32;`). Give it its value, or declare it with `var` and a type and assign it later. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#names-types-and-flow-n0200%E2%80%93n0299) |
| N0221 | error | A `var` has neither a type nor an initialiser (`var c;`). Write one of them. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#names-types-and-flow-n0200%E2%80%93n0299) |
| N0222 | error | A generic function or type does not check for the type arguments it is used with, and no other error says why. Use type arguments that the generic's body can work with. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#names-types-and-flow-n0200%E2%80%93n0299) |
| N0224 | error | A call that returns `void` is used as a value (`let d = nothing();`), or a `let` takes an expression of type `never`. Write the call as a statement. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#names-types-and-flow-n0200%E2%80%93n0299) |
| N0225 | error | An expression that is not a call is used as a statement (`1 + 2;`), so its value is lost. Use the value, or remove the statement. | [3.3](./ch03-03-functions) |
| N0226 | error | `void` is used other than as a return type (`var e: void;`), or `never` other than as a function's return type. Use them only there. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#names-types-and-flow-n0200%E2%80%93n0299) |
| N0227 | error | A struct holds itself by value, directly or through other structs, so its size would have no end. Put the inner value in a `Box`. An interface that is its own supertrait gives this too. | [15.1](./ch15-01-box) |
| N0228 | error | Two members of one type have one name - two fields, a field and a method, an associated constant and another member, or a function of an enum and a variant. Rename one. | [5.3](./ch05-03-methods) |
| N0229 | error | A struct literal leaves out a field (`Point { x: 1 }`). Give every field a value. | [5.1](./ch05-01-defining-structs) |
| N0230 | error | A field the struct does not have, in a literal or an access (`p.z`), or a method named where a field is needed. Check the name - the message suggests members that exist. | [15.5](./ch15-05-shared-ownership) |
| N0231 | error | A struct literal gives one field twice. Remove one. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#names-types-and-flow-n0200%E2%80%93n0299) |
| N0232 | error | `this` is used in a function that is not a method, or a `this` parameter is declared outside a type. Use `this` only in methods. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#names-types-and-flow-n0200%E2%80%93n0299) |
| N0233 | error | A method is called on the type (`Point.sum()`), or a static function on a value (`p.origin()`). Call a method on a value, and a static function on the type's name. | [5.3](./ch05-03-methods) |
| N0234 | error | A field, a method or a struct literal is used on a type that has none - a number, a type parameter no bound of which declares the method, or an optional, which has only `isSome` and `isNull`. Take the value out of the optional first, or add the bound. | [9.3](./ch09-03-allocation-failure) |
| N0235 | error | A block that is a branch of an `if` or `match` expression ends with a statement, so it has no value. End the block with its value, without `;`. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#names-types-and-flow-n0200%E2%80%93n0299) |
| N0236 | error | A closure's type cannot be inferred - a parameter has no type, or a block body returns a value, where no function or closure type is expected (`let f = (x) => x + 1;`). Write the parameters' types. | [13.1](./ch13-01-closures) |

## Borrows (N0240 to N0249)

The borrow checker's diagnostics. It runs only on a program that type-checks, and its errors carry notes that say where the borrow was taken and where it is used later. The messages say "reference" for a borrow.

| Code | Kind | What went wrong, and the usual fix | Shown in |
|---|---|---|---|
| N0240 | error | A place is assigned, or moved, while a borrow of it is used later. Finish with the borrow first, or copy the value you need out of it. | [4.2](./ch04-02-borrowing), [13.1](./ch13-01-closures) |
| N0241 | error | A borrow conflicts with a borrow that is still in use - two `borrow mut` of one place, or a `borrow mut` while a shared borrow lives. Finish with the first borrow before you take the second. | [4.3](./ch04-03-slices-and-views), [8.1](./ch08-01-vectors), [8.3](./ch08-03-maps), [12.4](./ch12-04-test-first), [13.2](./ch13-02-iteration), [15.3](./ch15-03-allocators), [16.1](./ch16-01-starting-threads), [17.2](./ch17-02-scopes) |
| N0242 | error | A place is read while a `borrow mut` of it is still in use. Read through the borrow, or after its last use. | [4.2](./ch04-02-borrowing) |
| N0243 | error | A value goes out of scope, or a temporary ends with its statement, while a borrow of it is used later. Bind the value to a local that lives long enough. | [4.3](./ch04-03-slices-and-views), [10.3](./ch10-03-regions), [13.3](./ch13-03-project-improved) |
| N0244 | error | A function returns a borrow of one of its own locals or of a temporary, which ends when the function returns. Return the value itself, or borrow from a parameter. | [10.3](./ch10-03-regions), [21.2](./ch21-02-requests-and-responses) |
| N0245 | error | A function that returns a borrow does not say rightly which parameters the result borrows from - the `borrow(...)` list is missing where there are several candidates, or leaves out a parameter the result comes from. Name the sources in the return type, `-> borrow(a, b) T`. | [10.3](./ch10-03-regions), [12.4](./ch12-04-test-first), [13.1](./ch13-01-closures), [15.3](./ch15-03-allocators) |
| N0246 | error | A borrow is in a place that cannot hold one - a struct field, a constant, a `var` local, or a borrow of a borrow. Own the value in that place, or keep the borrow in a `let` local. | [15.1](./ch15-01-box) |
| N0247 | error | `borrow` is applied to something that is not a place, such as a literal or a call's result (`borrow 5`, `take(mut five())`). Bind the value to a local first. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#references-and-borrows-n0240%E2%80%93n0249-lifetimes-md) |
| N0248 | error | `borrow mut`, or a method that takes `borrow mut this`, is used on something that cannot change - a `let` local, a parameter or a shared borrow. Declare the local with `var`. | [5.3](./ch05-03-methods), [16.3](./ch16-03-shared-state), [18.1](./ch18-01-dynamic-dispatch), [21.1](./ch21-01-one-connection) |
| N0249 | error | An argument lacks `mut` where the parameter is `borrow mut`, or has `mut` where the parameter is not. Write `f(mut x)` for a `borrow mut` parameter, and only there. | [2](./ch02-00-guessing-game) |

## Moves, destruction, `match` and arrays (N0250 to N0259)

The move checker also runs only on a program that type-checks. A move of a value that is borrowed is N0240.

| Code | Kind | What went wrong, and the usual fix | Shown in |
|---|---|---|---|
| N0250 | error | A value is used after it was moved, on at least one path, or a struct is read as a whole after one of its fields was moved. A note says where the move was. Pass a borrow in place of the move, or do not use the value again. | [4.1](./ch04-01-what-ownership-is), [5.1](./ch05-01-defining-structs), [5.2](./ch05-02-example-structs), [5.3](./ch05-03-methods), [10.1](./ch10-01-generic-types), [16.1](./ch16-01-starting-threads), [16.2](./ch16-02-channels), [19.3](./ch19-03-the-syntax-whole), [20.1](./ch20-01-unsafe-code), [21.3](./ch21-03-thread-pool) |
| N0251 | error | A value that is not Copy is moved out of something reached through a borrow (`let a = r.a;` with `r` a borrow). Borrow the part in place of moving it. | [8.1](./ch08-01-vectors), [13.2](./ch13-02-iteration), [22.2](./ch22-02-kernel-code) |
| N0252 | error | A field is moved out of a value whose type has a `drop` block, which needs the whole value when it runs. Borrow the field. | [15.2](./ch15-02-destruction) |
| N0253 | error | A `using` binding is moved. It is destroyed at the end of its block, so borrow it. | [15.2](./ch15-02-destruction) |
| N0254 | error | `return`, `break`, `continue`, `defer` or `?` is inside a deferred statement. A deferred statement runs to its end, so handle an error inside it. | [15.2](./ch15-02-destruction) |
| N0256 | error | A `match` does not cover every value of what it matches. Add the missing variants or a `_` arm. An arm with a guard does not count. | [3.5](./ch03-05-control-flow), [6.2](./ch06-02-match), [18.2](./ch18-02-when-to-use-it), [19.2](./ch19-02-patterns-that-can-fail) |
| N0257 | error | A `match` arm can never run - its pattern repeats an earlier one, or it comes after `_`. Remove it, or move it up. | [6.2](./ch06-02-match), [19.2](./ch19-02-patterns-that-can-fail) |
| N0259 | error | An array that cannot exist - a length that is not a constant of at least 1, an element type that is not Copy (`[Res; 2]`), more than 2^31 − 1 bytes, or `[]` where no slice is expected. Also `fill`, `copyFrom`, `extend` or `resize` with elements that are not Copy. Use a `Vector` for such elements, and for a length known only at run time. | [8.1](./ch08-01-vectors) |

## Results, the heap, generics and interfaces (N0260 to N0268)

`Result`, optionals and allocators, and what generic code and `impl` blocks must satisfy.

| Code | Kind | What went wrong, and the usual fix | Shown in |
|---|---|---|---|
| N0260 | error | `Ok(…)`, `Err(…)` or `null` stands where nothing fixes its type (`let a = Ok(1);`, `let n = null;`), or where another type is expected. Give the variable a type. | [6.3](./ch06-03-optionals), [9.2](./ch09-02-result) |
| N0261 | error | `?` is in a function that cannot return what `?` would pass on - the function does not return a `Result` with the same error type, or an error enum with an `@from` variant for it, or `?` is on an optional and the function does not return an optional. Change the return type, convert the error, or handle it with `match`. | [9.2](./ch09-02-result), [12.2](./ch12-02-reading-a-file), [12.3](./ch12-03-refactoring), [15.2](./ch15-02-destruction), [17.4](./ch17-04-async-io) |
| N0262 | error | `?` or `!` is on a value that is not a `Result` or an optional, or the left side of `??` is not an optional. Remove the operator. An `@from` variant without exactly one payload gives this too. | [11.1](./ch11-01-writing-tests) |
| N0263 | error | An allocator argument is not an allocator type (`Box<i32, Point>`). Use `SystemHeap`, `FailingAllocator`, or a struct without fields that implements `Allocator`. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#results-and-the-heap-n0260%E2%80%93n0269-type-system-md-%C2%A717%E2%80%93%C2%A718) |
| N0264 | error | A value that an arena or a scratch frame cannot hold - one that needs a drop, or a scoped value such as a borrow. Allocate only plain data there. | [15.3](./ch15-03-allocators) |
| N0265 | error | The type arguments of a generic call, a struct literal or an enum value cannot be worked out from its arguments (`let d = Maybe.Nothing;`, `let e = make();`). Write them, `make<i32>()` - the type the call's result goes to is not used. | [10.1](./ch10-01-generic-types) |
| N0266 | error | Generic instantiation is nested more than 64 deep, as when a generic function calls itself with a larger type each time. Remove the recursion in the types. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#results-and-the-heap-n0260%E2%80%93n0269-type-system-md-%C2%A717%E2%80%93%C2%A718) |
| N0267 | error | An `impl` does not match its interface, or cannot exist - a method is missing, extra, or differs in its receiver, a parameter or the return type, the `impl` is repeated or overlaps another, or it is outside the package of both its interface and its type. Make each method agree with the interface's declaration. | [10.2](./ch10-02-interfaces), [18.2](./ch18-02-when-to-use-it), [20.3](./ch20-03-more-interfaces-and-generics) |
| N0268 | error | A type argument does not meet a bound of its type parameter - it does not implement the interface, or is not `Copy`. Implement the interface for the type, or use a type that has it. | [8.3](./ch08-03-maps), [10.2](./ch10-02-interfaces), [15.4](./ch15-04-cells), [18.1](./ch18-01-dynamic-dispatch), [20.3](./ch20-03-more-interfaces-and-generics) |

## Regions (N0270 to N0274)

A region parameter says what a struct, an enum or a function's result borrows from.

| Code | Kind | What went wrong, and the usual fix | Shown in |
|---|---|---|---|
| N0270 | error | A struct or enum has a field or payload of a scoped type, such as `StringView` or a borrow, and no region parameter. Declare one, `struct S<region r>`, or hold an owned value such as a `String`. | [10.3](./ch10-03-regions), [12.3](./ch12-03-refactoring) |
| N0272 | error | A function stores a value that holds a borrow through a `borrow mut` parameter, and its signature does not say the borrow may go there (`v.push(s)` with `v: borrow mut Vector<StringView>`), or it stores one in a `static mut`. The signature must say that the parameter may hold what the stored value borrows from. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#region-parameters-n0270%E2%80%93n0279-type-system-md-%C2%A725-m6x) |
| N0273 | error | A region name that nothing declares, region arguments on a type without region parameters or the wrong number of them, or `static` in a parameter's type. Declare the region, `<region r>`, and use it. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#region-parameters-n0270%E2%80%93n0279-type-system-md-%C2%A725-m6x) |
| N0274 | error | A scoped type such as `StringView` is the type argument of a generic that needs an unscoped one, because it boxes the value or makes an array of it. Pass an owned type. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#region-parameters-n0270%E2%80%93n0279-type-system-md-%C2%A725-m6x) |

## Unsafe code and raw pointers (N0280 to N0283)

What may be written only in `unsafe`, and what raw pointers may point to.

| Code | Kind | What went wrong, and the usual fix | Shown in |
|---|---|---|---|
| N0280 | error | An unsafe operation outside an unsafe context - a read or write through a raw pointer, a call of an `unsafe fn` or of a C function, a `fromRaw` function, or a use of a `static mut`. Put it in an `unsafe { … }` block, in a function whose doc comment has a `Safety:` line. | [20.1](./ch20-01-unsafe-code), [20.2](./ch20-02-calling-c), [22.2](./ch22-02-kernel-code) |
| N0281 | error | A raw pointer to a type it cannot point to - a borrow, a slice, a `StringView` or another scoped type, or `never`. Point to the value itself. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#unsafe-and-raw-pointers-n0280%E2%80%93n0289-type-system-md-%C2%A727-unsafe-md-m8a) |
| N0282 | error | An operation the raw pointer does not allow - a write through a `*T` (it needs a `*mut T`), a read or write of a type that is not Copy, or any access through `*void`. Use a pointer of the right type. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#unsafe-and-raw-pointers-n0280%E2%80%93n0289-type-system-md-%C2%A727-unsafe-md-m8a) |
| N0283 | error | An `unsafe fn`, or a function that contains `unsafe`, has no doc comment with a `Safety:` line. Add `/// Safety: …` above it, saying why the code is sound. | [20.1](./ch20-01-unsafe-code) |

## C, profiles, effects and closures' kinds (N0290 to N0299)

Attributes, the C boundary, the freestanding profile, effects, `private`, and functions as values.

| Code | Kind | What went wrong, and the usual fix | Shown in |
|---|---|---|---|
| N0290 | error | An attribute that does not exist, is in the wrong place, is repeated or has wrong arguments (`@inline fn f() {}`), a `@derive` of anything but `Equal`, `HashKey` and `OrderKey`, an ABI other than `"C"`, or an extern declaration with a body. Use the attribute as its section shows it. | [20.5](./ch20-05-derives-and-macros) |
| N0291 | error | A type that cannot cross to C is in an extern declaration, an `@export` function or a `@repr(C)` struct, such as a slice or a `Box`. Pass a raw pointer and a length, or a `@repr(C)` struct. | [14.3](./ch14-03-libraries-for-other-programs), [20.2](./ch20-02-calling-c), [22.3](./ch22-03-inside-a-host-program) |
| N0292 | error | A C name that C does not allow or that CeeSafe keeps for itself - not an identifier, a C keyword, or one that starts with `ceesafe_`, `cee_` or `CEE_`. Choose another name. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#c-interoperability-and-profiles-n0290%E2%80%93n0299-type-system-md-%C2%A728-m8b-profiles-md-%C2%A74-m8c) |
| N0293 | error | Under `--profile freestanding`, the code names something that needs an operating system (`Console`, `Process`, `File`, the heap and the collections that use it), or declares `main`. Use the parts of the library the profile has, or build for the hosted profile. | [22.1](./ch22-01-the-freestanding-profile) |
| N0294 | error | An imported C type whose size CeeSafe does not know is used by value - as a parameter, a result, a field or an element - or is read, written or stepped over through a pointer. Use it only through a raw pointer. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#c-interoperability-and-profiles-n0290%E2%80%93n0299-type-system-md-%C2%A728-m8b-profiles-md-%C2%A74-m8c) |
| N0295 | error | An operation has an effect (`sleep`, `alloc`, `suspend`) its context forbids - a blocking call in an async function, a call beyond a function's `@effects` list, or one in `@context(atomic)` or `@context(irq)` code. In async code use the async form, such as `AsyncConsole`, and elsewhere move the operation out. | [17.4](./ch17-04-async-io), [17.5](./ch17-05-tasks-and-threads), [21.4](./ch21-04-async-tasks), [21.5](./ch21-05-graceful-shutdown), [22.2](./ch22-02-kernel-code) |
| N0296 | error | A `private` field or item is named outside the source file that declares it. Use it only in its own file, or remove `private`. | [7.2](./ch07-02-files-and-public), [11.3](./ch11-03-organising-tests) |
| N0297 | error | A float type, a float literal or `fromBits` is in a build with `--no-float`. Use integers. | [22.2](./ch22-02-kernel-code) |
| N0298 | error | A function that cannot be a value is used as one - an `extern` or `unsafe` function, one with region parameters, `main`, or an async function. Pass a closure that calls it. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#c-interoperability-and-profiles-n0290%E2%80%93n0299-type-system-md-%C2%A728-m8b-profiles-md-%C2%A74-m8c) |
| N0299 | error | A closure of the wrong kind for the type expected - one that captures where a plain `fn` is expected, one that changes what it captures where a `borrow fn` is expected, or one with effects the expected type does not list. Change the parameter's type to the kind of closure you pass. | [13.1](./ch13-01-closures) |

## Build (N0300)

Reported by `ceesafec build`, not by `ceesafec check`.

| Code | Kind | What went wrong, and the usual fix | Shown in |
|---|---|---|---|
| N0300 | error | `ceesafec build` is to make an executable, and the program has no `main` function. Add `fn main()`, or make the package a library. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |

## Names across packages (N0310 to N0315)

Names that one package uses from another.

| Code | Kind | What went wrong, and the usual fix | Shown in |
|---|---|---|---|
| N0310 | error | An `import`, or a struct literal `p.T { … }`, names a package that is not a dependency of this one. Add it under `[dependencies]` in `ceesafe.toml`, or correct the name. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0311 | error | A dependency has no item of that name (`geometry.Pointt`). Check the spelling. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0312 | error | An item of another package, or a field or method of one of its structs, exists and is not `public`. Mark it `public` in its package, or use what is public. | [7.2](./ch07-02-files-and-public) |
| N0313 | error | A name written without its package is provided by two imports. Write `package.Name`. | [7.3](./ch07-03-imports) |
| N0314 | error | A `public` item's signature names a type that other packages cannot see. Make that type `public` too. | [7.2](./ch07-02-files-and-public) |
| N0315 | error | An item or a type parameter has the name of one of the package's dependencies. Rename it. | [7.3](./ch07-03-imports) |

## Packages (N0320 to N0329, N0335)

The manifest `ceesafe.toml`, the lock file `ceesafe.lock`, dependencies, versions and publishing. These are reported at a line of the manifest or the lock file, not of a source file.

| Code | Kind | What went wrong, and the usual fix | Shown in |
|---|---|---|---|
| N0320 | error | `ceesafe.toml` or `ceesafe.lock` is not valid in the subset of TOML that CeeSafe reads, for example a string without quotes. Correct the line the message names. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0321 | error | A field of the manifest is missing, unknown or has a value it cannot have (`kind = "binary"`), or a dependency is an executable. `kind` is `"executable"` or `"library"`. | [7.1](./ch07-01-package-and-manifest), [7.4](./ch07-04-dependencies) |
| N0322 | error | A path dependency's directory or its `ceesafe.toml` is missing, or the package there has another name than the key. Correct the path or the key. | [7.4](./ch07-04-dependencies) |
| N0323 | error | A git dependency cannot be fetched or resolved, or is not in the cache when `--offline` is given. Check the address and the tag, and run `ceesafec fetch` with a network. | [7.4](./ch07-04-dependencies) |
| N0324 | error | `ceesafe.lock` is missing, or does not match the manifest. Run `ceesafec fetch`. | [7.4](./ch07-04-dependencies) |
| N0325 | error | A fetched dependency's manifest and sources do not match the hash in `ceesafe.lock`, as when a file in the cache was edited. Put the files back as they were fetched. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0326 | error | One package name is reached through two different sources. Make every package that depends on it name the same source. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0327 | error | Packages depend on each other in a cycle. Remove one of the dependencies. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0328 | error | A version, a version requirement or an index entry is not valid (`shapes = "1.x"`). Write a version as `1.4.0`, and a requirement such as `^1.0`. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0329 | error | No version of a dependency satisfies every requirement on it. The message lists the requirements that conflict and where each comes from, so loosen one. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0335 | error | `ceesafec publish` refuses the package as it is, for example with a path dependency or with changes that are not committed. The message says what to change. | [14.2](./ch14-02-publishing) |

## Later rules (N0330 to N0364)

The codes of the features that came after the groups above were numbered - `dyn`, owning closures, threads, statics, async, tests, cells, const parameters, patterns, `debugAssert`, embedded files and the package cache. The specification lists them in one table under "Build".

| Code | Kind | What went wrong, and the usual fix | Shown in |
|---|---|---|---|
| N0330 | error | `dyn I` is used as a value's own type - a local, a parameter, a field, an element or a type argument. Put it behind a borrow or in a box, `borrow dyn I` or `Box<dyn I>`. | [18.1](./ch18-01-dynamic-dispatch) |
| N0331 | error | `dyn I` for an interface that cannot be used so - a method takes `this` by value, has no receiver, has type parameters or names `Self`, or the interface has an associated type or a constant, or requires `Copy`. Use a generic with a bound. | [18.1](./ch18-01-dynamic-dispatch) |
| N0332 | error | A `move` closure captures a scoped value - a borrow, a view, a slice or a closure - which it could outlive. Capture an owned value, such as a `String` in place of a `StringView`. | [16.1](./ch16-01-starting-threads) |
| N0333 | error | A `move` closure literal stands where no owning closure is expected (`let f = move (x: u64) => x;`). Write it directly as the argument of `Box.create` where a `Box<dyn fn…>` is expected. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0334 | error | A value that is not `Send` must cross to another thread - a capture or the result of a spawned closure, or the argument of a `Send` bound - such as a `StringView` or a borrow. Move an owned value, or share one with `Arc`. | [15.5](./ch15-05-shared-ownership), [16.4](./ch16-04-send-and-share), [17.5](./ch17-05-tasks-and-threads) |
| N0336 | error | `@effectsOf` names no parameter, or a parameter that is not of a function or closure type. Name a parameter that is a closure. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0337 | error | A `static` that cannot be one - its type is not `Share`, or it is generic, or it is declared inside a function. Use a `Share` type, such as an atomic or a `Mutex`, at the top level. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0338 | error | A `static`'s initialiser, or the body of a `@constant` function, is not something the compiler can evaluate before the program runs (`static N: u64 = compute();`). Use literals, constants and struct literals. | [22.2](./ch22-02-kernel-code) |
| N0339 | error | `offsetOf<T>(field)` where `T` is not a struct, or has no field of that name. Name a struct and one of its fields. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0340 | error | `callerAddress()` is outside the body of an `@export` function, or in a closure inside one. Call it only in the exported function itself. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0341 | error | `await` is outside an async function or async closure, or in a `drop` block or a deferred statement. Make the function an `async fn`, or run the task from ordinary code with `Async.run`. | [17.1](./ch17-01-tasks-and-await) |
| N0342 | error | A task is made and not used - an async function is called without `await` (`let t = fetch(url);`), or `await` is given something that is not a task. Write `await f()`, or hand the call to `Async.run` or to a scope's `spawn`. | [17.1](./ch17-01-tasks-and-await) |
| N0343 | error | An async function awaits itself, directly or through other calls, where its frame cannot hold itself - in the freestanding profile, or through a `race` or `all` child. Write the recursion as a loop. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0344 | error | A child of an `Async.scope` captures a local of the scope's own body, which ends before the child does. Declare the local outside the scope, or make the child `async move` so that it takes the value. | [17.2](./ch17-02-scopes) |
| N0345 | error | `Async.park()` or `Async.waker()` is in a program. They are for the library only. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0346 | error | A member of an imported C union has a type some bit patterns of which are not values, such as `bool`. Use integers, raw pointers, or arrays of them. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0347 | error | An argument that goes through the `...` of a C variadic function has a type C would change or cannot take, such as `u8`, `bool` or `f32`. Convert it to `i32`, `u32`, `i64`, `u64`, `isize`, `usize`, `f64` or a raw pointer. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0348 | error | A `@test` function of the wrong shape - a method, with parameters, generic, exported, or returning anything but `void` or `Result<void, E>` - or a test called from the program's own code. Write `@test fn name()`. | [11.1](./ch11-01-writing-tests) |
| N0349 | error | A child spawned into a task set captures a value that holds a borrow - a borrow, a slice, a `StringView` - and may outlive the code that started it. Give the child owned values. | [17.2](./ch17-02-scopes) |
| N0350 | error | Something declared `@cfg("X")` - a C function, an imported field or an export - is used outside an `if (cfg("X")) { … }` block. Put the use inside one. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#warnings-n0400%E2%80%93n0499) |
| N0351 | error | A `Cell`, `RefCell` or `RawCell` holds a type that holds borrows (`RefCell<StringView>`), so its contents could outlive what they borrow. Put an owned type in the cell. | [15.4](./ch15-04-cells) |
| N0352 | error | A const parameter has a type it cannot have (`fn f<const X: f64>()`). Use `bool`, an integer type or an enum without payloads. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0353 | error | A const argument or an array length is not a constant - a local, a parameter, a call, or an expression over a const parameter (`[u8; N + 1]`). Use a literal, a constant, or the const parameter alone. | [20.3](./ch20-03-more-interfaces-and-generics) |
| N0354 | error | A generic argument of the wrong kind - a type where a const parameter needs a value (`Grouped<u32>`), or a value where a type is needed (`Vector<true>`). Give each parameter its kind. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0355 | error | A `match` guard moves, assigns or mutably borrows the matched value or one of the arm's bindings, or awaits. A guard only reads, so do that work in the arm's body. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0356 | error | The alternatives of an or-pattern bind different names, or one name with different types, as `Some(x)` and `null` in one arm do. Make every alternative bind the same names, or write separate arms. | [19.3](./ch19-03-the-syntax-whole) |
| N0357 | error | A range pattern matches nothing - `lo..=hi` with `lo` above `hi`, or `lo..hi` with `lo` not below `hi`. Put the bounds in order. | [19.2](./ch19-02-patterns-that-can-fail) |
| N0358 | error | A pattern names a constant that cannot be a pattern - anything but an integer or a `bool`, such as an `f64` - or a range pattern's bound is a name that is not a constant's. Bind the value and compare it in a guard, `x if (x == HALF) =>`. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0359 | error | An `e is P` test binds names where the test is not known to be true - under `!` or a logical or, or as a whole `let` initialiser or argument. Make it a condition of an `if` or `while`, or use `match` or `let … else`. | [19.1](./ch19-01-where-patterns-go) |
| N0360 | error | A `debugAssert` whose condition or message does more than read - it assigns, moves, does I/O, calls C, or exits - which a release build, where the assertion is left out, would not do. Compute the value in a statement before, and assert on that. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0361 | error | A file given to `embedText` is not UTF-8. Use `embed`, which gives the bytes. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0362 | error | A path given to `embed` or `embedText` cannot be embedded - it is not a string literal or a constant, is absolute, names no file, names a file over 16 MiB, or leads outside the package's directory and its `[embed] roots`. Use a relative path inside the package. | [14.1](./ch14-01-build-settings), [21.2](./ch21-02-requests-and-responses) |
| N0363 | error | Two source files of a `build --split` have paths that differ only in the case of their letters, which the file systems of macOS and Windows take as one file. Rename one. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |
| N0364 | error | A dependency, or a package it depends on, has errors. `check` reports it once, at the line of `ceesafe.toml` that leads to it - `ceesafec check --package NAME` shows that package's own diagnostics. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#build-n0300%E2%80%93n0399) |

## Warnings (N0400 to N0404)

A warning is printed as `warning[N0400]`. It never stops `check`, `build`, `run` or `test`, and never changes the exit status, unless the command has `--deny-warnings`, which makes each warning an error ([9.2](./ch09-02-result), [14.1](./ch14-01-build-settings)). Warnings are given for your own package's files only, never for a dependency's.

| Code | Kind | What went wrong, and the usual fix | Shown in |
|---|---|---|---|
| N0400 | warning | A string literal has `{name}`, and `name` is a variable in scope. CeeSafe has no string interpolation, so the braces are printed as written. Write the value in a call of its own, or `\{` where you mean a brace. | [1.2](./ch01-02-hello-world), [8.2](./ch08-02-strings), [14.1](./ch14-01-build-settings) |
| N0401 | warning | `name.x` where `name` is a local with the name of a dependency that has a public item `x`. The local hides the dependency there, so rename the local if you mean the package's item. | [the specification](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/diagnostics#warnings-n0400%E2%80%93n0499) |
| N0402 | warning | A call whose value is a `Result` is used as a statement, so an error it reports is lost (`v.push(1);`). Handle it with `?`, `!` or `match`, or discard it with `let _ = …;`. The same code warns of a `RefCell` guard that is still live at an `await`. | [8.1](./ch08-01-vectors), [9.2](./ch09-02-result), [9.3](./ch09-03-allocation-failure), [11.1](./ch11-01-writing-tests), [16.2](./ch16-02-channels), [17.1](./ch17-01-tasks-and-await), [21.1](./ch21-01-one-connection) |
| N0403 | warning | A `move` closure changes a captured variable of a Copy type, and the function reads the variable after the closure. The closure changed its own copy, so the read sees the old value. Share the value, with an atomic for example, or return it from the closure. | [16.1](./ch16-01-starting-threads) |
| N0404 | warning | A pattern after `is` or in a `let … else` is `_` or a plain name, which matches every value, so the test is always true and the `else` block never runs. Write a pattern that can fail, such as `Some(n)`, or a plain `let`. | [19.2](./ch19-02-patterns-that-can-fail) |

## Codes that are not given

The catalog has three codes that release %ceesafec-version% never reports. They are listed so that every code `ceesafec explain` knows is on this page. A code is never used again for another meaning.

| Code | Status |
|---|---|
| N0002 | Unassigned. No release has given it. |
| N0223 | Unassigned. No release has given it. |
| N0258 | Retired. It was given for a payload that is not Copy bound by a `match` on a value. Such a `match` now moves the payload out and consumes the value. |
